learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate analysis and synthesis capacity.
Demonstrate planning, organization and strategy skills.
Acquire the capacity for effective problem-solving.
Express oneself correctly in Spanish, both orally and in writing.
Possess knowledge of Information and Communication Technologies.
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis and processing within their field of application.
Develop the ability to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Information search and management skill.
Possess decision-making capacity.
Develop critical reasoning.
Develop interpersonal skills.
Develop teamwork capacity.
Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team.
Acquire commitment to ethics and social responsibility.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training.
Develop the capacity for adaptation to new situations.
Capacity to generate new ideas (creativity).
Ability to work autonomously.
Show initiative and entrepreneurial spirit.
Become aware of issues related to the environment.
Capacity to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of science, technology and chemistry of materials.
Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Know the chemical principles of matter, chemical reactions, and the chemistry of materials and the environment.
Acquire the basic knowledge of Chemistry necessary to address more specific aspects in other subjects of the degree, which they will develop in later years, and in subsequent professional practice.
Familiarize the student with analytical methods aimed at exercising quality control of various types of materials and the environment.
Relate environmental processes with chemical substances and chemical processes that constitute their fundamental basis.
Apply basic principles of Chemistry to Engineering.
Know the chemical nature of matter.
Express concentrations of substances in aqueous solution in different magnitudes and perform their conversions.
Quantify the effects of colligative properties in aqueous solutions.
Perform calculations based on the stoichiometry of chemical reactions.
Know how to correctly apply the principles of limiting reactant, direct and inverse yield, purity of substances, and moisture content in chemical reaction calculations.
Solve basic problems of Chemical Thermodynamics.
Know how to apply the principles of Chemical Equilibrium and the factors that influence its displacement.
Acquire basic knowledge of Chemical Kinetics and the factors that influence reaction rate.
Solve pH calculations in simple aqueous solutions.
Determine solubility and ionic concentrations in simple solutions.
Perform calculations of redox potentials and concentrations of chemical species in simple oxidation and reduction reactions.
Evaluate the factors that influence corrosion processes of different metals.
Understand the peculiarities and industrial applications of colloidal dispersions.
Address the knowledge of Environmental Chemistry of Water, and contaminants in aqueous media, with resolution of conceptually simple problems.
Know the dynamics of natural compounds and pollutants in the Atmosphere, their fundamental processes and the resolution of simple quantitative problems.
Know the basic principles and rules of working in the Chemistry Laboratory.
Foster the relationship between theoretical knowledge of Chemistry and its practical application through the realization of different Laboratory experiences.

syllabus_topics: UNIDAD I: FUNDAMENTAL CHEMISTRY
Topic 1: Chemical bond, chemical reactions and stoichiometry
Composition of Matter. Atomic and molecular concepts.
Chemical bonding: ionic, covalent, metallic and intermolecular bonds.
Ways of expressing the concentration of solutions. Types of chemical reactions.
Balances and calculations in chemical reactions: stoichiometry.
Theoretical and experimental yield. Limiting reactant.
Topic 2: Solutions and colloidal systems
Nature and type of solutions. Colligative properties: molecular and electrolyte solutions.
Topic 3: Thermodynamics, chemical equilibrium and chemical kinetics.
Chemical applications of the 1st and 2nd principles of Thermodynamics: enthalpy of formation and enthalpy of reaction.
Chemical Equilibrium. Displacement of Equilibrium: Le Chatelier's principle.
Chemical kinetics. Reaction rate: concept and influencing factors.
UNIDAD II: EQUILIBRIA IN AQUEOUS SOLUTION
Topic 4: Acid/base, precipitation and complexation equilibria
Acid/base equilibria: strength of acids and bases. Concept of pH.
Calculation of pH of different solutions: acids/bases, salts, buffer solutions.
Acid-base titration curves. Dissolution/precipitation equilibria: solubility product, Modification of solubility.
Topic 5: Oxidation-reduction equilibria and electrochemistry.
Electrode potentials and their measurement. Standard reduction potentials.
Galvanic cells. Electromotive force. Nernst equation.
Electrolytic cells. Faraday's Law.
UNIDAD III: ENVIRONMENTAL CHEMISTRY
Topic 6: Water
Water: importance and properties. Composition of natural waters.
Water contamination. Contamination indicator parameters.
Water quality criteria.
Topic 7: The atmosphere
Composition of the atmosphere. Air quality criteria.
Main atmospheric pollutants. Global problems: greenhouse effect, ozone layer depletion, acid rain.

assessment_methods.method: Public presentation of a work (in group)

assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 3.5 is required in each continuous assessment test, group work presentation, and laboratory practices to average with other tests. Students who do not meet this minimum must take a final exam to recover the failed parts, again requiring a minimum of 3.5. Attendance to a minimum of 80% of laboratory practices is compulsory. All evaluation tests are mandatory; failure to complete any results in a failing grade. For exceptional evaluation, the final grade is 40% from a theoretical and problem exam, 30% from a laboratory practices exam, and 30% from an individual work presentation.
